title: What If the Whole World Put Lead in Its Fuel? For a Century, It Did

scenes.text: What if the entire world burned lead in its gasoline? For almost a century, it did.
In the 1920s, engineers added tetraethyl lead to stop engines from knocking. Every car then breathed lead into city air.
Lead harms the developing brain. A 2022 study estimated Americans alive in 2015 lost about 824 million IQ points to childhood lead exposure.
The United States phased leaded fuel out of road cars by 1996, and children's blood lead levels fell sharply.
Algeria was the last country to stop selling it, in July 2021. In August, the United Nations declared leaded petrol gone worldwide.
The UN estimates that ending it prevents over a million early deaths every year and saves about 2.4 trillion dollars.

description:
What if the entire world burned lead in its gasoline?
From the 1920s, tetraethyl lead was added to petrol to stop engines knocking, spreading lead through the air of every city. A 2022 study estimated that Americans alive in 2015 lost about 824 million IQ points to childhood lead exposure. The US removed lead from road fuel by 1996, Algeria sold its last leaded petrol in July 2021, and the UN estimates the global phase-out prevents more than a million premature deaths a year.
